draft.title: Naming the sides of a right-angled triangle
card: Hypotenuse
The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.
Opposite
The opposite side is directly across from the angle you are using. It does not touch that angle.
Adjacent
The adjacent side is next to the angle you are using. It is the side that touches the angle and is not the hypotenuse.
Example: in triangle \(ABC\), the right angle is at \(C\). The hypotenuse is \(AB\). For angle \(A\), the opposite side is \(BC\) and the adjacent side is \(AC\). For angle \(B\), they swap.
draft.remember: The hypotenuse stays the same. Opposite and adjacent change with the angle you choose.

a.q: In triangle \(PQR\), the right angle is at \(Q\). Which side is the hypotenuse?
opts: The longest side next to angle \(P\)
a.why: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. The right angle is at \(Q\), so the side across from it is \(PR\). \(PQ\) touches the right angle, so it cannot be the hypotenuse.
a.clue: Which side is across from the right angle?

b.q: In triangle \(DEF\), the right angle is at \(E\). Taking angle \(F\) as the angle you are using, which side is the opposite side?
b.why: The opposite side is across from angle \(F\), so it is \(DE\). \(EF\) is tempting, but it touches angle \(F\), so it is the adjacent side. \(DF\) is the hypotenuse.
b.clue: Find the side that does not touch angle \(F\) and is not across from the right angle.

wants.why: Seeing the sides placed around angle A shows which side is opposite and which is adjacent.
